UK SMP CALCULATOR 2026/27 · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

How much Statutory Maternity Pay does your employee get?

Enter the expected due date, average weekly earnings and when employment started. You get the qualifying week, whether the 26-week and earnings tests are met, the week-by-week 39-week schedule and the matching Statutory Paternity Pay.

Written from the published rules without a live lookup. Rates and rules change; GOV.UK and HMRC decide. Not legal, payroll or employment advice.

What it does, and what it leaves to you

    
    
      
  • Covers: the qualifying week (15th week before the expected week), the 26-week continuous employment test, the lower earnings limit, the 39-week SMP schedule with the April uprating applied week by week, and the 2-week SPP amount.
    • 
      
  • Gives: an eligibility verdict, weekly and total pay, and a text file you can keep with the payroll record.
    • 
      
  • Not decided: how average weekly earnings are built from the 8-week period (bonuses, back-pay, pay rises), notice and evidence rules, adoption and shared parental pay, contractual schemes, Maternity Allowance, and leave rights. Your payroll provider or HMRC decides these.
    • 
    

  


  

    
Common questions

    
How much is Statutory Maternity Pay in 2026/27?

    
SMP is 90% of average weekly earnings for the first 6 weeks, then the lower of the standard weekly rate (about £194.32 from April 2026) and 90% of earnings for 33 weeks, 39 weeks in all. Check GOV.UK for the current rate.

    
Who qualifies for SMP?

    
An employee with 26 weeks of continuous employment ending with the 15th week before the expected week of childbirth, earning at least the lower earnings limit on average in the 8 weeks to that point.

    
When can SMP start?

    
No earlier than 11 weeks before the expected week of childbirth.

    
What if the employee does not qualify?

    
They may be able to claim Maternity Allowance from Jobcentre Plus.

    
Is my data uploaded anywhere?

    
No. Everything is calculated in your browser and nothing is sent.
